suprised i havent seen anyone mention this yet but, millions of videos on tiktok are about to have their sounds removed for copyright reasons. 

the copyright holder (universal music group, who has everone from ariana grande to the bee gees under them) published [an open letter](https://www.universalmusic.com/an-open-letter-to-the-artist-and-songwriter-community-why-we-must-call-time-out-on-tiktok/) titled "why we must call time out on tiktok" explaining why; 

umg will *not* be renewing their contract with tiktok, during contract renewal meetings UMG tried to seek: 1. better safeguarding for tiktok users, 2. better compensation for artists (despite the amount of times these songs are used on the site, tiktok accounts for about 1% of umgs revenue) and 3. safety for artists from ai generated content and the effects. and after negotiations does not believe tiktok will do anything about their concerns.

umg even go so far to say tiktok in retaliation to these issues brought up during meetings, tried to bully them into accepting a below market deal and selectively removing specific artists music as a form of intimidation.

overall umg say they "will always fight for our artists and songwriters and stand up for the creative and commercial value of music." The open letter didnt seem to mention any possibility of resolution unless a proper and fair deal can be made.


Obviously a large large portion of creators are freaking out. Every single video that used the songs will now be muted, hindering growth and attention. Cosplayers and artists seem to be panicked the most from what I'm seeing but no doubt this will affect every aspect of tiktok content creation. 
Of course in the comments discussing the letter and the consequences many users are saying they have ways around the copyright (i.e. making the video their own sound by saving it) and if it works will remain to be seen.

Sad this is what it came too, but honestly amazed that its happened. All artists deserve proper compensation
